title: Trump Demands Ukraine Swap Leaders as He Blames Zelenskyy for Soaring U.S. Fuel Prices
snippet: President Donald Trump called for a leadership change in Ukraine, accusing Volodymyr Zelenskyy of refusing to negotiate with Russia and blaming him for high U.S. diesel prices following a controversial energy agreement with Moscow.
content:
WASHINGTON — In a sharp escalation of international tensions, President Donald Trump declared Saturday that Ukraine needs a new leader, accusing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of prolonging the war with Russia and holding him responsible for skyrocketing U.S. diesel prices.

Speaking to reporters before departing for a campaign event in Tennessee, Trump criticized Zelenskyy’s diplomatic stance and urged Kyiv to halt strikes on Russian energy infrastructure.

"I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal, because he could have made many deals and for some reason he never does," Trump said. "He wants to make problems for the world. He wants to make problems for our farmers, our ranchers, with diesel fuel."

A Controversial Deal with Moscow

Trump's comments come on the heels of a surprise deal struck Friday with Russian President Vladimir Putin to purchase millions of tons of Russian diesel. The move is widely seen as a bid to tame soaring energy costs at home ahead of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections. To justify the agreement, Trump has blamed Ukrainian military action on Russian oil assets for domestic price hikes, brushing aside the broader economic fallout from ongoing military conflicts in the Middle East.

The agreement represents a dramatic pivot from recent sanctions legislation passed by Congress, which aimed to cut off the very energy revenues funding Moscow's military campaign.

Outrage in Kyiv Amid Fatal Bombings

The announcement met swift outrage in Ukraine, coming on the same day Russian glide bombs slammed into residential structures in the Zaporizhzhia region, killing at least 20 people, including three children, and injuring nearly two dozen others.

Zelenskyy forcefully condemned the arrangement in a statement posted on social media, pointing directly to the lethal strikes as evidence of Moscow's intentions.

"Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia," Zelenskyy wrote on X, adding that revenue from fuel sales directly finances Russian weapons, drone upgrades, and troop recruitment.

European Allies Voice Dismay

European leaders reacted with alarm to the Washington-Moscow pact, warning that bypassing energy restrictions undermines Western efforts to cripple the Kremlin’s war economy. Officials from Sweden and Germany reaffirmed their dedication to existing sanctions, while Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski publicly questioned Russia's capacity to deliver the promised fuel given recent damage to its domestic refineries.

The announcement also appears to have blindsided Ukrainian diplomats. U.S. envoys had met with a Ukrainian delegation in Miami just hours earlier to discuss potential peace frameworks, but Ukrainian officials confirmed they were given no prior warning of the U.S.-Russia diesel deal.
